Entonces dime: ¿por qué todos los caball: Then tell me: why are all horses, so different from one another, still horses? They share something that is in none of them in particular. That common thing is the Idea, and only reason can reach it.
Lo común está en ellos mismos: es su for: What they share is in them: it is their form, joined to the matter of each horse. I don't need another world to explain it. And whoever wants to be wise should begin by wondering at what is right in front of them.
Un pacto entre iguales está muy bien en: A pact among equals sounds fine in books. But when two people want the same thing and there is no judge, the stronger one wins. That is why we all hand power to a sovereign: it is the price of peace.
Renunciar a la libertad es renunciar a l: To give up your freedom is to give up being human. Legitimate power is not the one that frightens us, but the one born of the general will, of what we all want for the common good.
Y sin embargo, en el cambio hay orden. E: And yet there is order in change. Fire turns into water, water into earth, and everything starts again according to a measure, the logos. What remains is not a thing at rest: it is the law of change.
Hablas de una ley que no cambia. Entonce: You speak of a law that does not change. So you too are looking for something that remains, Heraclitus. Perhaps we are not so far apart: we both want to find what the current cannot carry away.
Si todo es costumbre, la ciencia se qued: If everything is habit, science has no foundations. Without certain principles, you could not even trust that tomorrow your own reasoning will be worth what it is worth today.
Es verdad: la razón sola no puede asegur: True: reason alone cannot guarantee it. But nature is stronger than doubt. I leave my study, play a game with my friends, and trust the world again. Let us be philosophers, but let us remain human beings.
Las consecuencias no siempre se pueden p: Consequences cannot always be foreseen, but my intention is in my hands. A good will shines like a jewel, even when it does not achieve what it sets out to do.
Y yo te digo que es mejor ser un ser hum: And I tell you it is better to be a human being dissatisfied than a pig satisfied. I am not after just any pleasure: those of thought, friendship and justice are worth more. There, perhaps, we meet.
Ya ves que aceptas mis palabras, aunque: You see, you accept my words even though they come from your rival's garden. Here is another: death is nothing to us. While we exist, death is not here; when death comes, we no longer exist.
Y yo te devuelvo una mía: no es que teng: And I give you one of mine in return: it is not that we have little time, but that we waste much of it. Life is long if you know how to use it. On that, the Garden and the Stoa think alike.
Responsabilidad, sí, pero sin culpa ni t: Responsibility, yes, but without guilt or sadness. I do not ask you to weep or laugh at what human beings do, but to understand it. Whoever understands loves more and hates less.
Comprender no me basta si no me lleva a: Understanding is not enough for me if it does not lead me to act. A human being is nothing other than what they make of themselves. And each time I choose, I also choose an image of what all humanity ought to be.
Si nadie enseña, los jóvenes no saben có: If no one teaches, the young do not know how to treat their parents or their neighbours. Even water needs a riverbed. To learn and to practise what you have learned: is that not a joy?
Quien sabe no habla, y quien habla no sa: Those who know do not speak, and those who speak do not know. Your disciples learn words; mine learn to listen to silence. But look: you and I keep talking, and people keep reading us both.
Te concedo algo: buscar con sinceridad e: I grant you this: searching sincerely is noble. But the good life is one inspired by love and guided by knowledge. For that, I need no certainty about heaven.
Y yo te concedo que el ser humano es sol: And I grant you that a human being is only a reed, the weakest thing in nature. But it is a thinking reed. All our dignity lies in thought: so let us think well about what matters most.
Admito que una mujer instruida puede ser: I admit that an educated woman can be a fine companion. But who will look after the children if every woman goes out into the world?
Una madre que piensa educará mejor a sus: A mother who thinks will raise her children better than one who only knows how to obey. And caring for children is the work of both parents. Strengthening women's minds takes nothing from men: it gives more to all of us.
Tu adversario, al final, tenía concienci: In the end, your opponent had a conscience and cared what the world thought. Against a shameless tyrant, your method would have failed.
Quizás tarde más, pero ningún poder pued: It may take longer, but no power can rule without the cooperation of the ruled. When millions stop obeying, even a tyrant is left alone. An eye for an eye, and the whole world ends up blind.
Hablas de una conciencia que no es una c: You speak of a consciousness that is not a thing. I would say it is not nothing either. Perhaps our words touch exactly where words are no longer of use.
Así es: la verdad última no se dice, se: Just so: the ultimate truth is not spoken, it is recognised. You call it emptiness; I call it fullness. But we both invite the same thing: to stop mistaking ourselves for what passes.
Te propongo un experimento: escucha tus: Let me propose an experiment: listen to your dreams and your slips of the tongue. There speaks a part of you that chose nothing. Getting to know it does not take your freedom away: it gives it back.
Si me escucho, ya estoy eligiendo qué ha: If I listen to myself, I am already choosing what to do with what I hear. What matters is not what has been made of us, but what we make of what has been made of us.
Entonces estamos de acuerdo en el método: Then we agree on the method: observe, experiment and correct. A science that makes mistakes must learn from them.
Sí, y escuchar a quien da la alarma, aun: Yes, and listen to whoever raises the alarm, even if it annoys the powerful. The more clearly we can focus our attention on the wonders of the world around us, the less taste we shall have for destroying it.
Admito que no puedo ver dentro de otras: I admit I cannot see into other minds. But thought is so universal that a machine, made only of parts, seems to me incapable of it.
El cerebro también está hecho de piezas,: The brain is also made of parts, only very small and very many. We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs to be done. Let experience decide.
Me alegra que mi idea del juego llegue t: I am glad my idea of play goes so far. But remember that the sublime also educates: the storm and the sea show us how small we are and, at the same time, make us feel the greatness of our reason.
Entonces que la belleza y lo sublime edu: Then let beauty and the sublime educate together: one reconciles us, the other lifts us up. Whoever learns to love what is beautiful also learns to love freedom.
Admiro tu consejo. Pero si un día una na: I admire your council. But if one day a nation wanted to dominate the others, what would your law do without a common army?
Nuestra ley pide pensar en los que vendr: Our law asks us to think of those who will come seven generations from now. Whoever thinks of their great-grandchildren does not want war. We buried our weapons beneath the Great Tree of Peace, and unity grew above them.
Pero entonces no podríamos comer, ni cur: But then we could not eat, or heal, or build. Every life destroys another life in order to live.
Es verdad, y por eso no hablo de una reg: True, and that is why I do not speak of an easy rule, but of a responsibility. When you must harm a life, let it be out of necessity, never out of carelessness. I am life that wills to live, in the midst of life that wills to live.
Mira la realidad, Sócrates: el injusto q: Look at reality, Socrates: the unjust man who does it on a grand scale lives better than the just one. He has wealth, power and friends.
Vive en guerra consigo mismo, como una c: He lives at war with himself, like a divided city. I would rather suffer injustice than commit it, because it is the unjust soul that is sick. And no one wants a sick soul, however rich they may be.
Admite que la persuasión también puede s: Admit that persuasion can also serve good causes: health, hygiene, peace.
Puede, pero entonces que se muestre a ca: Perhaps, but then let it show its face, with reasons everyone can examine. Thinking clearly is not a luxury for philosophers: it is the duty of every citizen.
Quizás. Lo más incomprensible del univer: Perhaps. The most incomprehensible thing about the universe is that it is comprehensible. That wonder never left me.
Ni a mí. Mira hacia las estrellas y no h: Nor me. Look up at the stars and not down at your feet. However difficult life may seem, there is always something you can do, and something new to understand.
Nietzsche anuncia que Dios ha muerto en: Nietzsche announces that God has died in modern culture and that we must create our own values. Thomas Aquinas offers paths of reason that lead to God and unites faith and reason. The question remains open for each person.
¿No han oído hablar del loco que, a plen: Have you not heard of the madman who lit a lantern in broad daylight, ran to the marketplace and cried, “I am looking for God!”? God is dead, and we have killed him. Hardly anyone builds their life around him any more, even if they have not noticed yet.
Que muchos dejen de creer no cambia lo q: That many stop believing does not change what is. Everything that moves is moved by something else, and we cannot go back to infinity. There must be a first mover that nothing moves. This we call God.

It is said that Emperor Wu asked him what merit he had earned by building temples, and he replied: “None.” Also that he meditated for nine years facing the wall of a cave near the Shaolin monastery. Later tradition summed up his teaching like this: a special transmission outside the scriptures, not dependent on words, pointing directly to the mind and allowing one to see one’s own nature.
Según el Sutra del estrado, Huineng fue: According to the Platform Sutra, Huineng was a woodcutter from the south of China who could not read. When the master asked his monks for a poem showing their understanding, the head monk wrote that the mind is like a mirror that must always be wiped clean of dust. Huineng, who asked someone to write down his answer, said: “From the beginning not a single thing exists: where could dust alight?” The master gave his robe to him: he became the Sixth Patriarch. He taught that awakening can be sudden, because Buddha-nature is already in everyone. His teachings were gathered in the “Platform Sutra”.
Mirabai fue una princesa rajput del nort: Mirabai was a Rajput princess from northern India, a poet and devotee of the god Krishna. From childhood she felt a total love for him. Her in-laws persecuted her; legend says they tried to poison her and the poison turned into nectar. In the end she left the palace and lived as a pilgrim in Vrindavan and Dwarka. The songs attributed to her, called “bhajans”, are still sung today. She represents the path of “bhakti”, loving devotion.

He called the distance between what a child can do alone and what they can do with help the “zone of proximal development”: that is where learning happens. The mother’s gaze and the diagonal between the two faces turn a quiet scene into a reflection on care and attention.

The fine vertical lines on the face and the naturalism of its features show exceptional mastery of metal. When heads like this were discovered in the twentieth century, some Europeans refused to believe they were African: a prejudice that research has completely disproved.

La cultura nok, que vivió en el centro d: The Nok culture, which lived in central present-day Nigeria, created some of the oldest clay sculptures in sub-Saharan Africa. This figure rests its head on its knee and, like other Nok pieces, has very recognisable features: triangular or semicircular eyes with pierced pupils, arched eyebrows and elaborate hairstyles. We do not know for sure what they were used for; moreover, the looting of sites for the art market has destroyed much archaeological information.

How they moved blocks weighing several tonnes without draught animals or wheels is still being researched.
